title: Planned failback and traffic thermostat for model swap
author: Asha Menon
body: Context: Customers saw ephemeral post-swap latency spikes when a new model warmed up under real traffic. Motivation: provide a deterministic, observable, and reversible policy that smooths traffic shifts (the "traffic thermostat") and schedules a planned failback window if quality regressions are detected. Goals: 1) Avoid large instantaneous traffic jumps that overload caches/GPUs; 2) Provide a scheduled, auditable failback plan with automatic graceful rollback that preserves session-affinity; 3) Integrate with existing shadow-replay plumbing so we can validate candidate model outputs against baseline without impacting users. Summary of changes: Implements a traffic thermostat controller that phases traffic according to an adaptive temperature curve derived from latency, token-efficiency, and model-confidence signals. Adds a "planned failback" subcontroller which can register a future failback window (timeboxed) tied to a model swap; during the window the system monitors quality regressions against a user-supplied metric set and, if a run rate of violations exceeds the configured failure budget, triggers a graceful roll-back with preflight drain and snapshotting of in-flight sessions. The controller integrates with shadow-replay to build an ongoing disagreement histogram and with the console rollout timeline for visualization and operator overrides. API changes: new rollout policy fields (thermostat_profile, failback_window_minutes, confidence_thresholds, replay_sample_rate). Backwards compatibility: defaults are conservative and no change for existing rollout configs. Migration: CLI helper to annotate existing active swaps with a default thermostat_profile. Testing and safety: unit tests for scheduler logic, e2e test against the perf canary harness, and a short-term synthetic shadow-replay run in the benchmark-lab. Observability: adds two new metrics (rollout_thermostat_temperature and planned_failback_violation_count), plus dashboards and alerting playbooks. Rollout plan: staged canary in dev -> beta -> prod with a 6-hour observation window and manual approval gates after beta. Related: references ENG-1345 for thermostat tuning experiments, SUP-7823 incident postmortem. Docs: console rollout reference and a new runbook for planned failbacks. Merge notes: squash-merged after sign-off. This PR is targeted at production-safe defaults and includes opt-in knobs for aggressive rollouters.

review_comments: Diego Ramirez: Overall looks solid. Two concerns: 1) how thermostat interacts with autoscaler when temperature stays high for long periods; 2) snapshot size when failing back with many in-flight sessions. Please add documentation and a small test for both.
Author (Asha): Added autoscaler backpressure hook and documented snapshot retention. Snapshot size limited to metadata + causal checkpoints to avoid full state blowup.
Claire Ng: I'm worried about the default confidence thresholds being too permissive for multimodal models. Recommend lowering default and adding a checklist for teams to opt-in with overrides.
Author (Asha): Lowered default confidence threshold from 0.6 to 0.75 for multimodal model family and added CLI flag to revert if needed.
Michael O'Connor: CI flaked on e2e (timeout). Reran and passed; please monitor for flakiness in benchmark-lab harness.
Reviewer (Diego): Approved pending one minor log message change.
Author (Asha): Addressed log change and added structured log fields for rollout_id and thermostat_step.
release_notes: Adds a traffic thermostat controller to smooth model swaps, planned failback windows with automatic rollback on metric regressions, shadow-replay integration for disagreement analysis, and new rollout policy fields (thermostat_profile, failback_window_minutes, confidence_thresholds, replay_sample_rate).
risk_summary: Low-medium. Conservative defaults preserve existing behavior. The primary risk is misconfiguration by teams who opt into aggressive thermostat profiles; mitigations include a runtime guardrail, playbook, and canary observation windows.
manual_steps: 1) Optional: annotate existing swap via `rw rollout annotate --thermostat default` 2) Observe new metrics in console (rollout_thermostat_temperature, planned_failback_violation_count) 3) Use console timeline to cancel scheduled failback or to force immediate rollback if necessary.
notes_for_merger: Squash merge commit contains tests and docs; keep changelog entry and set the release target to next-minor. Ensure all dashboard panels are imported to prod observability namespace before release.
changelog_entry: feature: rollout: traffic thermostat and planned failback windows (ENG-1345)
additional_comments: Post-merge: schedule a 48-hour telemetry review with SRE to validate thermostat heuristics on low-latency clusters.
compliance_notes: No PII exposure changes. Snapshots avoid persisting user payloads by default.
testing_playbook: See tests/e2e/thermostat_canary_test.py and benchmark-lab harness steps in console/docs/rollout-thermostat.md
